name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz ~65% below normal; 11 ships hit to 6 Nov
summary: Hormuz traffic about 65% below pre-conflict levels per UKMTO; 11 ships attacked in the week to 6 Nov, three sunk
state: UKMTO's weekly report of 10 Nov counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound Hormuz transits, about 65% below pre-conflict levels, with at least 11 ships attacked in the week to 6 Nov and three sunk (Gulf News). A tanker fire near Khasab on 7 Nov was reclassified as an attack on 9 Nov, and Iranian state media said four tankers were halted in the strait over 24 hours (CBS News). Qatar was due to present an Iran-approved plan to reopen the strait in exchange for lifting the US blockade on 9 Nov; neither side has confirmed it (Iran International).
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf remains heavily disrupted, which keeps pressure on oil, gas and freight costs. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state advisories; travellers to the region should check FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded: ~65% below pre-conflict levels (UKMTO, 10 Nov)

sources.title: Gulf News — Hormuz shipping 'below normal, but not stalled': UKMTO

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
